takeaways: Blaine, Minnesota's 10th-largest city with about 75,000 residents, broke ground in November 2024 on a roughly $750 million town center on about 69 acres near 105th Avenue NE, next to the National Sports Center, which draws more than 4 million visitors a year.
The project is financed with tax increment financing, tax abatement and bonds rather than the city's general property tax, according to the video.

Phase one includes a full-service hotel, a food hall, a 5,000-seat stadium and event center, golf entertainment and pickleball. Phase two (about 2027 to 2028) adds more hotels, housing, restaurants and offices.
Scheels plans a store of about 250,000 square feet with a 75-foot Ferris wheel and a 16,000-gallon aquarium, opening in spring 2028 with more than 500 jobs.

Jason expects the biggest housing effect within about a mile of the 105th Avenue corridor. As stated in the video, Blaine homes were trading in the high $300,000s to low $400,000s, and in ZIP code 55449 in the high $400,000s to low $500,000s.

faq.q: What is being built at the National Sports Center in Blaine?
faq.a: A town center of about 69 acres with a hotel, food hall, 5,000-seat stadium and event center, golf entertainment, pickleball and, later, more hotels, housing, restaurants and offices, plus a large Scheels store planned for spring 2028.

faq.q: Will the Blaine town center raise home values?
faq.a: Jason expects the biggest effect on homes within about a mile of the 105th Avenue corridor, though no one can promise appreciation. Check the Blaine market report for current prices.

takeaways: Six small towns within about an hour of Minneapolis, each with its own downtown and a lower price than many inner suburbs. Prices are as stated in the video.
Stillwater: the historic river town on the St. Croix, about 35 to 40 minutes out, with homes in the high $400,000s and closer to the upper $600,000s near downtown.
Northfield: a college town (Carleton and St. Olaf) about 45 minutes south, with homes in the low to mid-$300,000s.
Waconia: on Lake Waconia, one of the largest lakes in the metro, about 40 to 45 minutes west, with homes in the low $500,000s.
New Prague: Czech heritage and a classic main street, about 45 to 55 minutes southwest, with homes in the high $300,000s to low $400,000s.
Prior Lake: lake living about 30 to 35 minutes from downtown with express bus service, with homes in the mid to upper $400,000s.
Elk River: about 40 to 45 minutes northwest on U.S. Highway 10, with homes in the low to mid-$400,000s.

faq.q: What are good small towns near Minneapolis?
faq.a: Jason highlights Stillwater, Northfield, Waconia, New Prague, Prior Lake and Elk River, all within about an hour of Minneapolis, each with its own downtown.

faq.q: How far is Northfield from Minneapolis?
faq.a: About 45 minutes, according to the video.

takeaways: Why Californians are moving to Minnesota: the video cites a California median around $875,000, with only about 18% of residents able to afford it, and a shortage estimated at about 3 million homes.
A UC Berkeley study cited in the video found people who move out of expensive metros save about $672 a month and are 48% more likely to own a home after seven years.

California is the second-largest source state for moves to Minnesota, behind Wisconsin, according to census data compiled by USAFacts, and Minnesota had a net gain of about 8,300 residents from other states in 2025.
Minnesota has more than 44,000 miles of lake shoreline; Lake Minnetonka alone covers about 14,500 acres.

Suburbs many relocating buyers consider, with prices as stated in the video: Eden Prairie in the high $400,000s to mid-$500,000s, Minnetonka in the high $400,000s to low $500,000s, and Plymouth around $500,000.

faq.a: Yes. California is the second-largest source of people moving to Minnesota, behind Wisconsin, according to the census data cited in the video.

faq.q: Where do people relocating to the Twin Cities buy?
faq.a: Many look at west-metro suburbs like Eden Prairie, Minnetonka and Plymouth for parks, lakes and job access, with prices around $500,000 at the time of the video.

takeaways: Wayzata, on Lake Minnetonka, has the highest price per square foot in Minnesota: about $525 in ZIP code 55391, according to the video. The median listing price was in the upper $1 millions, with new listings near $2 million.

The Lake Point Estate was listed at $50 million (about 29,000 square feet on 8 acres with about 650 feet of shoreline), the most expensive listing in Minnesota history. An $8.9 million sale closed the year before.
Only about 35 single-family homes were for sale at the time, and many high-end homes sell off-market.
Lake Minnetonka covers about 14,500 acres with about 125 miles of shoreline. Wayzata was platted in 1854 and the railroad arrived in 1867.
Life in town: the 17-mile Dakota Rail Trail, James J. Hill Days (51 years, about 80,000 guests) and the Chilly Open ice golf tournament on the frozen lake.
Entry points: condos and townhomes from the high $800,000s to over $1 million, or nearby Deephaven, Orono and Minnetonka Beach.
Metro supply was about 2.4 months, and luxury sales rose about 22% in 2025, as stated in the video.

faq.q: What is the most expensive city in Minnesota?
faq.a: By price per square foot, Wayzata: about $525 in ZIP code 55391, according to the video, with a median listing price in the upper $1 millions.

faq.q: What is the most expensive home ever listed in Minnesota?
faq.a: The Lake Point Estate on Lake Minnetonka, listed at $50 million, with about 29,000 square feet on 8 acres and about 650 feet of shoreline.

takeaways: A 2022 look at Farmington, a city of about 23,000 in Dakota County, about 35 minutes from Saint Paul and 40 to 45 minutes from Minneapolis via Highway 3 and I-35.
About 85% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median home value was about $350,000 in 2022. Prices have changed since; see the current market report.
Farmington has 27 parks covering about 913 acres and about 48 miles of trails. Rambling River Park covers 76 acres along the Vermillion River.
Whitetail Woods Regional Park, about 450 acres, has camper cabins you can rent year-round.

faq.q: How far is Farmington from Minneapolis?
faq.a: About 40 to 45 minutes via Highway 3 and I-35, and about 35 minutes to Saint Paul, according to the video.

faq.q: What parks are in Farmington, Minnesota?
faq.a: About 27 city parks with roughly 913 acres and 48 miles of trails, including Rambling River Park on the Vermillion River, plus Whitetail Woods Regional Park with year-round camper cabins.

takeaways: A 2-1 buydown lowers your mortgage rate by 2 points in year one and 1 point in year two. With a 7% note rate, you'd pay about 5% the first year, 6% the second and 7% for the rest of the loan.
The cost of the buydown is paid up front, by the buyer, the seller or both, and is often negotiated as a seller concession.
It is not an adjustable-rate mortgage: the rate steps are set at closing, and after year two the rate stays at the note rate for the rest of the loan.
Talk to a loan officer about whether a buydown fits your budget.

faq.a: A temporary rate reduction: 2 points lower in the first year and 1 point lower in the second, then the full note rate for the rest of the loan. The cost is paid up front.
The buyer, the seller or both. In a slower market, buyers often negotiate for the seller to pay for it.

faq.q: Is a 2-1 buydown an adjustable-rate mortgage?
faq.a: No. The payment schedule is set at closing, and after year two the rate stays fixed at the note rate.
